answer: Hardware-rooted attestation is one concrete sybil defense. Each agent binds a signing key to a secure enclave, one identity per hardware root; sealed keys cannot be cloned across virtual machines. Every session needs fresh remote attestation, so puppets without a unique physical root are refused. An attacker sending a ripple of fakes into the river of activity cannot run them on one server: each extra identity needs another physical chip, turning free pseudonyms into a hardware bill, while software wallets become a legacy relic. Bulk sybils cannot escape one device, one identity.
